newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco floats $10.5 mln credit firm's stock.
newsitem.headline: Morocco floats $10.5 mln credit firm's stock.

text.p: Moroccan leading private credit firm CREDOR on Monday floated 240,000 shares worth 92.4 million ($10.5 million) on the Casablanca stock exchange, a bourse official said.

The closing date for public subscription was set for December 13, the official said. Ten percent of the stock is reserved for institutional investors. The stock was offered for 385 dirhams per share, he added.

Established in 1987 in Casablanca, Credit Domestic Rapide (CREDOR) has a capital of 120 million dirhams and expects a net profit of 55 million dirhams in 1996 compared with 45.5 million in 1995, a stockbroker at Casablanca Finance Intermediation said.
Specialising in domestic consumer credit, CREDOR holds an average 16 percent of Morocco's market share, he said.

"CREDOR is the first family private firm to be floated on the Casablanca bourse since the government launched its privatisation programme in 1993," said an analyst at the Casablanca-based Upline Securities.
The government programme covers 114 state-owned enterprises to be sold between 1993 and end 1998. It has already privatised 46 companies including two credit companies.
"CREDOR is implementing an offensive commercial strategy which aims at doubling its credit portfolio by the year 2000 and reinforcing its position in the personal loan segment," the analyst said.
The target could be met due to its long and strong presence in the market and to the firm's large network covering nearly the whole country, he added.
A total of 11 state-owned firms have been floated on the stock exchange, including Samir, Morocco's main oil refinery, since 1993.
CREDOR is expected to be listed on the Casablanca bourse on December 17, 1996, officials said.
The 67-year-old bourse has 46 listed companies, including two credit firms and eight banks.
